# Requirements Quality Checklist: Commit Message and Signature Enforcement

**Purpose**: Validate `spec.md` as an instrument — completeness, clarity, consistency and testability of the requirements themselves, not of any implementation of them
**Created**: 2026-09-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the committed location that holds the categories, scope policy and length limit named, or only described as "one committed location"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for what the message check does with a message that is empty, or that consists only of comment lines git will strip? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for how the outgoing range is determined when a branch is being pushed for the first time and has no remote counterpart? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for a push that deletes a ref, where there are no commits to examine? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec state what happens when the checks are active but the repository has no signing identity configured at all, distinct from a commit merely being unsigned? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for the state query when the checks were activated and then deactivated by hand? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the disposition record for a declined skill-review finding required to be durable, or may it exist only in conversation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK008 Are requirements stated for what the activation command must do when it finds a conflicting hook configuration already in place? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK009 Is "verifiable authorship signature" defined precisely enough that a reader can decide any given commit without consulting the implementation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "structurally valid but cannot be checked against a known key" distinguishable from "fails validation" by a stated criterion rather than by example? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary of "machine-generated" fixed to the four named cases, or open to others the tooling may produce? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "the documented emergency route" singular or plural — FR-015 says "each bypass route", FR-015 and §US1 scenario 4 say "the documented emergency route"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "non-empty description" specified as to whether leading or trailing whitespace counts toward it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004a]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "72 characters" defined in terms of characters, bytes, or display columns, given that a description may contain non-ASCII text? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "short identifier" quantified, or left to the reader? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK016 Do FR-005 (exempting machine-generated messages) and FR-001 (examining every commit message) state their relationship, or must the reader infer which wins? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK017 Do FR-012 (arrange for commits to be signed at creation) and the non-goal "issuing, distributing or rotating signing keys" leave a gap where signing is arranged but no key exists? [Conflict, Spec §FR-012, §Non-Goals]
- [ ] CHK018 Are FR-014 (exit non-zero on the first rule broken) and FR-007 (list every offending commit) consistent, given that stopping at the first violation and enumerating all of them are different behaviours? [Conflict, Spec §FR-007, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK019 Do the Assumptions and FR-006 agree on whether an unverifiable signature is acceptable, and is the reasoning stated once rather than twice? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK020 Do §US3's "installed no additional tooling" and §US3 scenario 4's optional third-party hook manager describe one requirement or two? [Consistency, Spec §US3]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK021 Can SC-001 ("100% of commits ... satisfy the stated convention") be measured without re-running the check over history, and is the measurement window defined? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK022 Is SC-003's "under one minute" attributable to the command's runtime, the contributor's reading time, or both? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK023 Can SC-004 ("no contributor needs to read a script") be objectively verified, or is it a judgement? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK024 Is SC-006's verification procedure — comparing identifiers across a refused then permitted send — stated precisely enough to execute? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK025 Does every functional requirement trace to at least one acceptance scenario or success criterion? [Traceability]
- [ ] CHK026 Are FR-016 through FR-018 (documentation) covered by any acceptance scenario that could fail? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, §FR-017, §FR-018]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK027 Are primary-flow requirements complete for each of the five user stories? [Coverage]
- [ ] CHK028 Are exception-flow requirements stated for the activation command failing partway — some configuration written, some not? [Gap, Recovery]
- [ ] CHK029 Are recovery requirements defined for a contributor whose send was refused, beyond being told the remediation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK030 Are requirements stated for deactivating the checks, or is activation one-way? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK031 Are requirements defined for a working copy where a different hooks mechanism was already configured before activation? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements stated for the checks' runtime cost, given that they run on every commit and every push? [Gap, Performance]
- [ ] CHK033 Are the checks required to work when the repository is used through a graphical client that does not present hook output? [Gap, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements stated for what the checks may read or write outside the repository? [Gap, Security]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the prohibition on a package manager, virtual environment or install step (FR-010) stated as a testable condition or as an intent? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK036 Is the assumption that contributors have or will configure a signing identity validated anywhere, or only recorded? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the dependency on the repository's existing quality-gate scripts, documentation conventions and instruction files stated specifically enough to identify what would break? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the claim that the Angular category set matches existing history stated as evidence with a location, or asserted? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK039 Does the spec resolve whether "the send" means one ref update or the whole push invocation, when a push carries several refs of differing signature status? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK040 Is "the repository's distributed skills" bounded to a stated set, or left for the implementer to decide what counts? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-019]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK018 was raised against FR-014's original wording ("exit non-zero on the first rule they find broken"), which contradicted FR-007's requirement to list every offending commit. FR-014 was reworded in the same session to separate failing fast — which governs whether a later check runs after an earlier one failed — from enumerating within one check. The item is left unchecked for the reviewer to confirm the rewording actually resolves it.
- CHK017 is the other item most likely to need a spec edit rather than a reviewer judgement: FR-012 arranges for signing while the non-goals disclaim key provision, and nothing states what happens in the gap.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
